business_snapshot.title: Business snapshot
business_snapshot.content: IRCTC primarily focuses on serving passengers and travellers within India, with core operations centered on domestic train services, catering, tourism, and related services [3]. The company operates through four main business segments: Catering, Rail Neer, Tourism & Train Operation, and Internet Ticketing [9]. Its revenue mix is led by Catering contributing 46.00% of total turnover, followed by Internet Ticketing Services at 29.44%, Tourism at 17.07%, and Rail Neer at 7.49% [4].

trajectory.title: Trajectory
trajectory.content: The travel, tourism, online travel booking, and catering markets are projected to experience robust multi-year growth, driven by rising internet penetration, smartphone adoption, urbanisation, and government initiatives [1, 3, 6, 7]. IRCTC's own business segments, including marketing and ad revenue, loyalty programs, and overall tourism offerings, have shown strong ongoing increases [1, 10]. Conversely, margins in the IT business compressed due to the allocation of additional CSR expenses and direct costs [5].

balance_sheet.title: Balance sheet
balance_sheet.content: IRCTC maintains a low-leverage balance sheet with no bank borrowings, relying primarily on cash, cash equivalents, and operational cash flow for its liquidity needs. Its total debt to shareholder's equity ratio stood at 0.02 as of March 31, 2026, consistent with March 31, 2025, while its debt service coverage ratio improved to 57.92. Regarding working capital, the net capital turnover ratio was 1.53 on a standalone basis (1.52 consolidated) for FY2026 compared to 1.64 standalone (1.62 consolidated) in FY2025. The company considers its working capital sufficient for operational requirements, retaining surplus cash in short-term bank deposits.

guidance.title: Guidance
content: Management plans to add around 25% to 30% capacity in about 1.5 years through plant expansions and new installations [3].
Capacity expansion plans for existing Rail Neer plants include augmenting Ambernath from 2 lakh to 3 lakh bottles per day and Danapur from 1 lakh to 2 lakh bottles per day [5].
The board has sanctioned the installation of 4 new plants at Mysore, Prayagraj, Bhagalpur, and Ranchi [3].

bull: The internet ticketing segment maintains market leadership with an 89% share of reserved railway tickets, delivering robust profitability with high EBITDA margins (76% to 85%) driven by strong operating leverage and cost efficiencies [2, 3].
The catering segment achieved impressive year-on-year revenue growth of 26.84% (reaching Rs. 671 crores), while tourism revenue also grew strongly by 10.95% to Rs. 304 crores [2, 4].
bear: Overall company EBITDA margins have compressed down to roughly 27% to 28% from historical levels of 36% due to changes in the revenue mix, specifically a higher sales contribution from lower-margin train catering and tourism segments [1, 4, 8].
Profitability has been impacted by legacy items and increased costs, including the implications of advertising and pilot initiatives such as branded catering projects [2, 4, 8].
